subject: Post-call next steps: AcmeHealth pilot buying path — clearance for SLA & discount
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lena Gomez <lena.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps from today's pilot discovery — stakeholder map attached

Hi Sanjay / Lena,

Thanks again for a productive conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

- Goal: 8-week pilot to validate triage/notes summarization for ambulatory ops (target 2k monthly active patient notes).
- Success criteria: 1) 40% reduction in average documentation time for clinicians; 2) no PII exfiltration incidents; 3) throughput >= 20 req/s during peak shifts.
- Key stakeholders you called out: Clinical Ops (Sanjay), Procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com), Security (Lena).
- Procurement ask: rough budget window and procurement lead details so we can route SOW + pilot license.
- Security ask: KMS + SOC2 evidence; you mentioned your security team will want a KMS integration and a short questionnaire answered.

I attached a quick stakeholder map to capture roles and decision triggers. Also flagging two internal asks so we can move toward a signed pilot:
1) Pricing: they asked about a pilot discount. I can offer a promotional pilot discount but need internal clearance.
2) SLA: AcmeHealth asked for a 99.9% uptime commitment for the pilot window. That is outside our standard pilot SLO — requesting internal review if we can provide an SLA variance (or an alternative escalation/credit structure).

Immediate proposed next steps:
- Sanjay / procurement: send the procurement contact and target contract date.
- Acme security: send the short security questionnaire by EOD Friday.
- Internal: Marcus and Monica, looping you for pricing / legal signoff on the two asks above. I attached the stakeholder map and a draft pilot SOW for context.

Thanks — happy to jump on another 20-min sync if helpful.

Best,
Olga
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: AcmeHealth-stakeholder-map.xlsx, pilot-sow-draft.pdf
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, Lena Gomez <lena.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps from today's pilot discovery — stakeholder map attached

Hi Olga — thanks for the clear summary. Quick responses: 

- Procurement lead: Maria Torres (maria.torres@acmehealth.com). They run 30–45 day vendor onboarding cycles for pilots but we can accelerate with a procurement-approved PO or LOI.
- Security: I'll have Jenna in security send the questionnaire back; they will definitely want a KMS integration and evidence of SOC2 plus a short architecture diagram.
- SLA: The request for 99.9% is from our clinical ops head — their risk tolerance is high given potential patient-impact use cases. If Redwood can provide either a 99.9% uptime or a clear credit/escalation path, that will materially shorten our approval timeline.
- Budget: this pilot sits under an innovation fund with a target spend of ~$40k for the 8 weeks.

Attaching our procurement checklist (sent separately from procurement@acmehealth.com). Happy to do a quick procurement call with Maria if that helps.

—Sanjay
VP Clinical Ops, AcmeHealth
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Requesting clearance — 15% pilot discount + SLA variance (AcmeHealth / ACM-2026-07)

Marcus / Monica —

Following the call with AcmeHealth, they have two gating asks that will determine whether procurement routes this quickly:
1) Pilot discount: they're asking for meaningful pilot pricing to fit within a ~$40k innovation budget. I am proposing a one-time 15% pilot discount off our list pilot price for the 8-week engagement. This is promotional and limited to the pilot term only.
2) SLA variance: they asked for 99.9% uptime for the pilot. Our standard pilot offering does 99.5% (no credits). I'm requesting guidance if we can:
   a) Offer a temporary SLA of 99.5% + an operational escalation path (priority response + escalation within 2 hours) and warranty language in the SOW, or
   b) Approve a formal 99.9% SLA for the pilot with a limited credit schedule (requires legal signoff).

Attachments: SLA-exception-form.docx and pilot-sow-draft.pdf with the proposed pricing line.

If we can approve (a) today I can reply to Sanjay and Maria with procurement next steps and send the LOI for signature. If we consider (b) we'll need a short legal review and finance signoff on revenue recognition/credit exposure.

Quick ask: Please reply with green/amber/red and any conditions.

Thanks,
Olga
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Requesting clearance — 15% pilot discount + SLA variance (AcmeHealth / ACM-2026-07)

Olga — I appreciate the fast turnaround. My read: green on a pilot promo discount up to 15% provided we keep it time-boxed to the 8-week pilot and include a clear clause that production pricing will be re-negotiated. Finance should be notified but I don't expect major pushback at this level.

On SLA: amber. I'm OK with option (a) — keep SLA at 99.5% and offer an operational escalation path + credit ladder capped at 5% of pilot fees for any sustained failure. For option (b) (formal 99.9% SLA), we should only consider if: 1) legal signs off on the credit exposure and 2) we secure an enterprise commit or a path to conversion documented in the SOW.

Please route to Monica for legal redlines on the SOW/SLA language. If Monica approves (b) with a tight credit cap, we can proceed, but priority is to keep pilot contract simple to avoid procurement delays.

—Marcus
Head of Sales, North America
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Requesting clearance — 15% pilot discount + SLA variance (AcmeHealth / ACM-2026-07)

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the attached SLA-exception-form and pilot SOW draft. High-level notes: 

- Pilot discount: no legal issue. Ensure the discount is explicitly limited to the pilot term and that the SOW states standard rates apply post-pilot.
- SLA: we're not comfortable committing to a standing 99.9% uptime without deeper review of architecture and data residency. Option (a) is acceptable — 99.5% for the pilot + a documented escalation path and limited service credit schedule capped at 5% of pilot fees. We'll carve out KMS integration specifics and require that any KMS/HSM access model is written into the SOW (customer-managed keys preferred).
- Data & retention: provide specifics on retention windows and deletion flows for PHI. Our legal team will add standard security representations and a narrow liability cap for pilot engagements.

Action items for Olga:
1) Ask Acme for their security questionnaire answers and an architecture diagram (Jenna from security).
2) Prepare an SOW with the 15% pilot discount and SLA = 99.5% + escalation + capped credits. Attach a short KMS spec.
3) If the customer insists on 99.9%, advise them we'll need an enterprise purchase path and a legal review (longer timeline).

I'll attach a redline snippet to the SOW and the SLA-exception-form for your use.

—Monica
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: legal-sow-redline.txt
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmehealth.com>, Maria Torres <maria.torres@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Pilot offer & next steps — draft LOI and SOW (AcmeHealth)

Hi Sanjay / Maria — following internal review, quick update and proposed next steps so procurement can move forward: 

1) Pricing: We can offer a one-time 12% pilot discount (slightly below the 15% ask) for the 8-week pilot. Discount limited to pilot fees only; production pricing will be discussed after pilot completion.
2) SLA & credits: Pilot SLA will be 99.5% uptime. We will include a written escalation path (priority response within 2 hours) and a capped service credit schedule not to exceed 5% of pilot fees for sustained outages. Monica (legal) has added standard pilot liability and KMS specs — customer-managed keys preferred.
3) Security: please send Jenna's security questionnaire answers and an architecture diagram; we will return a completed SOC2/controls evidence package and a short KMS integration spec.
4) Procurement: if you can confirm Maria as the procurement lead, we will send a short LOI for signature (DocuSign link below) and the SOW with the pricing and SLA noted.

DocuSign LOI: https://www.docusign.com/loi/ACM-LOI-98765
Attachments: pilot-sow-draft.pdf (SOW with pilot scope, pricing, and timeline).

Proposed immediate next step: Maria, if you confirm procurement cadence we will send the LOI and jump on a 30-min procurement call early next week to finalize PO/LOI details.

Thanks — excited to move this forward.

Best,
Olga

Redwood Inference
